Pages (shared docs three-column layout: left nav / center body / right try-it or anchors) | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Docs home: Quickstart, Authentication, Idempotency, Pagination, Errors sections + Popular guides 4 cards | | `quickstart.html` | Install + first-charge two-step example | | `charges.html` | Charges API: Charge object 18-field table + 5 endpoint sections (POST create / GET single / capture / refund / list), each section with parameter table + multi-lang code block + JSON response example; right-column try-it panel syncs with the current endpoint as you scroll, fill params + Send returns a mock response (`currency=usd/eur/gbp/jpy` returns a charge object, anything else returns `currency_not_supported`) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full weaveapi system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The WeaveAPI documentation effectively provides an interactive 'Try It' panel and detailed API references, but suffers from severe mobile usability issues, including broken layouts with extreme horizontal overflow and inaccessible sidebars. Desktop navigation is hindered by anchor links hiding target headings behind the sticky header and buggy active-state highlighting in sidebars and code tabs. Note that only 40% of visible interactive features were exercised during this session, leaving a substantial portion of the interface—such as numerous sidebar anchor variations and potential form edge cases—untested.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and evaluate the UX of the WeaveAPI developer documentation, focusing on navigation, interactive API explorers, and responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by verifying global elements like the side navigation, search, dark mode, and code snippet tabs on the homepage. It will then proceed to the core API reference pages, specifically testing the interactive 'Try It' panel on the Charges page for state synchronization and mock response handling. Finally, the run will cover supporting pages (Customers, Webhooks, Errors) and perform a dedicated mobile viewport pass to check for layout overflows and tap target sizing.
assumptions: The search bar (ctrl+K) may be a visual mock or rely on a simple client-side filter.
The 'Try It' panel on charges.html contains mock logic specifically handling 'currency' values to return different JSON payloads.
Horizontal scrolling may be required for tables or code blocks on mobile viewports.
risk_hotspots: The right-column 'Try It' panel in charges.html (syncing with scroll position and handling form submissions)
Horizontal overflow in API parameter tables (charges.html, customers.html)
Small tap targets in the left navigation menu on mobile
Code block tab switching (CURL, PYTHON, NODE, GO)

findings.user_goal: Read and navigate the documentation on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The documentation pages fail to adapt responsively to mobile viewports, maintaining fixed layout widths that cause severe horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: Observed on multiple pages (index.html, charges.html, customers.html, quickstart.html, webhooks.html) where the page width remains around 880px in a 390px viewport. The left sidebar is entirely inaccessible, and text, code blocks, and tables are cut off.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices are forced to constantly pan horizontally to read content and cannot navigate between major sections, rendering the mobile experience largely unusable.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive CSS media queries to stack columns vertically on small screens, allow text content to wrap, hide the sidebar behind a toggleable hamburger menu, and restrict horizontal scrolling strictly to overflow containers for code blocks and wide tables.

findings.user_goal: Test API endpoints using the interactive console.
findings.problem: The 'Send →' button in the 'Try it' panel renders with invisible text.
findings.evidence: Noted during desktop exploration of charges.html: 'The "Send →" button in the right-side "Try it" panel renders as a solid purple block with invisible text'.
findings.why_it_matters: The primary call-to-action for the interactive console is unreadable, creating a severe accessibility barrier and causing confusion for users trying to figure out how to submit the mock request.
findings.suggestion: Update the CSS for the 'Send' button to ensure the text color (e.g., white) has sufficient contrast against the purple background.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to specific sections using anchor links.
findings.problem: Clicking anchor links scrolls the page such that the target heading is hidden underneath the sticky top search bar.
findings.evidence: Observed when clicking left and right navigation links (e.g., 'Authentication', 'Idempotency', 'Events'). The heading text lands behind the sticky header area.
findings.why_it_matters: Users lose context when jumping to a new section because they cannot see the title of the section they just navigated to, forcing them to manually scroll up.
findings.suggestion: Apply a 'scroll-margin-top' or 'scroll-padding-top' CSS property to anchor targets (headings or section wrappers) equal to or slightly greater than the height of the fixed header.

findings.user_goal: Understand current location within the documentation.
findings.problem: Active state highlighting in the sidebars is buggy, either highlighting multiple irrelevant links simultaneously or failing to update properly during scrollspy.
findings.evidence: On charges.html, clicking 'Bank' caused 'Charges', 'Cards', 'Bank', and 'Wallets' to highlight simultaneously. On webhooks.html, visiting a section caused all links under WEBHOOKS to display active styling.
findings.why_it_matters: Inaccurate orientational feedback confuses users about where they currently are in the documentation structure, especially when jumping between closely related endpoints.
findings.suggestion: Refine the JavaScript logic handling the 'active' class assignment. Ensure precise matching for hashes/paths, and for scrollspy implementations, verify intersection observer thresholds don't trigger multiple overlapping states.

findings.user_goal: Switch programming languages for code snippets.
findings.problem: When clicking a language tab (e.g., PYTHON, NODE), the code snippet content updates correctly, but the active visual highlight remains stuck on the previously selected tab.
findings.evidence: Observed repeatedly on quickstart.html and charges.html. For example, clicking 'PYTHON' updates the code, but 'NODE' or 'CURL' remains visually highlighted with a blue background.
findings.why_it_matters: The visual disconnect between the selected tab and the displayed code causes cognitive friction and lowers trust in the documentation's accuracy.
findings.suggestion: Update the tab-switching JavaScript event listener to correctly remove the 'active' class from all sibling tab buttons before applying it to the clicked target.

findings.user_goal: Toggle dark mode for better readability.
findings.problem: The dark mode toggle button (🌙) is completely non-functional.
findings.evidence: Tested multiple times on desktop and mobile viewports across different pages; clicking it produced no visual theme changes and the icon did not update.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expecting to reduce eye strain in low-light environments are left frustrated by a broken control that provides no feedback.
findings.suggestion: Implement the JavaScript handler for the theme toggle to apply a data-theme attribute or class to the body/html tag, and swap the icon to reflect the active state.

findings.user_goal: Search the documentation for specific terms.
findings.problem: The search input fails to trigger a dropdown, autocomplete suggestions, or visual filtering on pages other than the index, and fails entirely on mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: Typing 'refund' on charges.html or attempting to use search on mobile customers.html did not produce any visible results or dropdown UI.
findings.why_it_matters: Search is a critical fallback navigation method. When it breaks inconsistently across pages and devices, users are blocked from finding specific technical answers efficiently.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the search dropdown JavaScript is correctly initialized globally and binds to the search input element consistently across all HTML files and responsive viewports.

findings.user_goal: Interact with code snippets and settings on mobile.
findings.problem: Interactive elements like code block language tabs, copy buttons, and the theme toggle have heights ranging from 22px to 36px, which are below standard touch target recommendations.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings on webhooks.html (mobile) flag the 'CURL' tab (50x22px), 'Copy' button (48x24px), and theme toggle (36x36px) as small tap targets.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets lead to accidental clicks and user frustration on touch devices, particularly when trying to switch code examples tightly packed together.
findings.suggestion: Increase the minimum height and padding of these buttons to ensure they meet the standard 44x44px mobile touch target guideline.
